review: The carbon fibre lid feels sturdy and it survived a fall off my desk.
The display is fine for spreadsheets but looks dull next to an OLED.
Plenty of ports, two Thunderbolt, two USB-A and HDMI, so no dongles at all.
Very expensive for the specs, you are paying a lot for the ThinkPad name.
Speakers are thin and quiet, fine for calls but not for movies.
Incredibly light for a 14 inch laptop, I barely notice it in my backpack.
The keyboard is the best I have ever typed on, deep travel and a lovely feel.
Battery gets me through a normal workday of email, Teams and browsing.
Performance is snappy for office work and coding.
It gets warm on the left side during long video calls.
Professional look, great keyboard and no bloatware. Perfect business laptop.
The webcam is sharp but the privacy shutter is easy to leave closed by accident.
Lenovo onsite warranty was excellent, a technician replaced the fan within two days.
The TrackPoint is handy once you learn it, and the trackpad is smooth too.
Integrated graphics struggle with anything beyond light photo editing.
Rock solid for work, the fingerprint reader and IR camera log me in instantly.
